transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Well, I guess the main thing is, since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow myself down. I’m not going to a job anymore, but my body—or my head, maybe—still acts like I’ve got a whole crew waiting on me and a list of things that need doing right now.

I get up and I’m moving from one little job to the next all day. It might be something small, but I’m on to it before I’ve even really thought it through. Then I see something else, and then another thing, and pretty soon the day’s gone and I feel like I’ve been running around nonstop. It’s not that I’m doing anything big necessarily, but I’m constantly up, constantly busy, like I don’t know how to just sit still and be retired, I suppose. That’s really what brought me in.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic, maybe even like you didn’t need much sleep, and your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

I don’t know that I’d put it that way, exactly. I mean, I do feel like I’m always kind of keyed up and moving, but “unusually energetic” sounds like… I don’t know, like a burst or some big change, and I’m not sure that’s what I’ve noticed.

As far as sleep, I can’t really say I’ve had times where I felt like I didn’t need it. I still get tired. My mind can feel busy, sure, but whether that’s “racing faster than usual,” I’m not sure. It’s more like I have trouble settling, if that makes sense, rather than feeling like I’m running on no sleep and doing great.
Do you often feel restless or find it difficult to relax, even when there’s no pressing reason to be doing something?

Yes, I’d say that’s pretty much it. Even when there isn’t anything that really has to be done, I feel like I should be doing something. Since I stopped working, especially, I just don’t seem to have that ability to sit down and say, “Alright, that’s enough for today.”

I’ll get up and notice some little thing—maybe something around the house, or something out in the yard—and before I know it I’m on my feet doing that, and then I spot another thing halfway through, and I move on to that. It’s like I still have that old work feeling in me, like there’s a crew waiting or a job that’s going to fall behind if I don’t keep moving, even though there’s no actual pressure there anymore.

Relaxing is hard, I guess. I can sit for a bit, but my mind goes to what else could be done, and then I’m back up again. It’s not always productive, either. It’s more like I’m just constantly in motion.
Do you find it hard to focus on one thing for very long, or do you get distracted easily by things around you?

Yes, I do. I mean, I can start out meaning to stay with one thing, but it doesn’t take much to pull me off it. Like if I’m trying to paint something, or even just sit down and plan out a story idea, I’ll be focused for a little while, and then I hear a truck go by outside, or I suddenly think, “Oh, I meant to check something in the garden,” and my mind just goes right over there.

And then I’ve lost the thread of what I was doing. I’ll look back at the page or the painting and it takes me a bit to remember where I was, if I can get back to it at all. It’s not always some big interruption either—just a sound, or a thought, or noticing something out the window. It feels like my attention sort of jumps tracks before I’ve decided to move it.
Have you found yourself making decisions quickly without thinking them through, or doing things impulsively that you later regret?

Maybe not big decisions so much, but I do catch myself jumping in too fast when I’m talking with people. Like in the storytelling meetings I go to, someone will be explaining an idea or setting up what they mean, and before they’ve even finished the sentence I’ll answer or add what I think they’re getting at.

At the time it feels like if I don’t say it right then, I’ll lose the thought, or I’m just excited because I think I know where they’re going. But then a second later I realize, oh, I cut them off. And I feel bad about it, because I don’t mean to be rude or take over the conversation. I’ll sometimes try to pull back and say, “Sorry, go ahead,” but by then I’ve already interrupted the flow.

So yes, in that way I guess I do act before I’ve really thought it through. It’s not like I’m trying to make quick decisions all the time, but verbally, I can be too quick off the mark.
Do you often feel worried or anxious, even when there's no clear reason for it?

I’m not sure I’d call it worry, exactly. I mean, I have ordinary concerns like anybody does, but I don’t think I sit around feeling anxious for no clear reason. At least, that’s not something I’ve really noticed as a main problem.

Sometimes I might feel a little unsettled if there’s something specific on my mind, but if you’re asking whether I get that kind of nervous feeling out of nowhere, with no reason I can point to… no, I don’t think so. It’s more that I get kind of keyed up or unable to settle, but not necessarily worried in the sense of being afraid something bad is going to happen.
Have there been times when you felt down or depressed for several days in a row, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I don’t think so, not in the way you mean. I have slower days, sure, where I don’t feel like doing much, or I sort of putter around and don’t get started on anything. But I wouldn’t say I’m down for several days in a row, like depressed, or that I lose interest in the things I normally like.

Most of the time, if I don’t get around to painting or writing or gardening, it’s not because I don’t care about them anymore. It’s more like I just don’t quite get myself organized to begin, or I drift into something else. But the interest is still there. If I actually sit with it, I still enjoy it.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed stretches where everything feels pointless or I don’t enjoy things. At least not enough that I’d think of it as a main problem.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt you needed much less sleep than usual, and yet still felt rested or energetic?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, my sleep can vary a bit, like anyone’s, but I can’t remember a period where I was sleeping much less than usual and then somehow felt great or especially energetic from it.

If I don’t sleep enough, I usually notice it. I might be slower getting going or just feel off. I wouldn’t say I get by on very little sleep and feel rested. So, no, that doesn’t really sound like something that’s happened to me.
